process_steps.title: The Gap & Repetition Problem
process_steps.desc: Originally, the tiling didn't work at all. It was just a bunch of tile shapes with gaps, overlapping in a repeating sunflower pattern rather than matching tessellation.

process_steps.title: True Space-Filling Tessellation
process_steps.desc: Rebuilt the engine into a continuous Archimedean ribbon where inner and outer curves match identically with zero gaps. Modulated tile arc lengths by prime factors and added 2x2 and 3x3 recursive fractal subdivisions on prime keystones.

process_steps.title: Arbitrary Tile Limits & Presets
process_steps.desc: Added direct numeric input to allow expanding tile counts up to arbitrary numbers (up to 50,000), paired with quick presets, instant fill, and auto-fit viewport zoom.

process_steps.title: Voronoi Border Fix
process_steps.desc: The Voronoi pattern broke on refinement after ~100 steps at the border because of an arbitrary distance cull. Fixed via distance-sorted nearest neighbor clipping and local bounding capsules.

process_steps.title: Uncapped Deep Zoom
process_steps.desc: Removed the 35% zoom-out floor, enabling smooth cursor-centered continuous zoom down to 0.5% with level-of-detail rendering for thousands of tiles.

ideas.title: AI driven Habitica

ideas.description: Habitica is an app I tried using in the past. It allows completing habit based real life tasks to improve the in-game character. You can set your own goals, tasks, etc. Then you can join skill guilds and spend coin on items in-game to flex the real life habit progress. What was missing is the a more seamless experience that an AI could provide.

ideas.title: Board game instruction chat
ideas.tagline: If you have a rule question, ask instead of searching
ideas.description: Sometimes the rules are unclear on the first read, sometimes we argue over the rules. What if there was an authority with perfect knowledge of the rules and references to show them? I imagine some RAG based system so the question can be vague-ish. Focus on text rules, not the images.

ideas.title: Macau strategy RL

ideas.description: Macau is a card game I played a lot as a kid. It has simple enough rules, but high complexity that is hard to comprehend. I want to try find a good strategy for playing the game. There are some guides online, but Reinforcement Learning could probably optimise it. A bot I can test myself against would be great.

ideas.title: Planning roof meadow
ideas.tagline: Deciding which plants can grow a roof together
ideas.description: Though I've never been, I found out that many bus stops in Norway have meadows on their roofs. I've seen it in random spots around the world too. There is a big one in Athens, with a whole park on top of a 10 story structure containing a beautiful library. But with constraints of being a roof, what plants can grow on top of it together? Maybe there is a way to plan it using data, and produce a seed mix that grows effortlessly according to other preferences..

ideas.title: Using foliage as a roof
ideas.tagline: A guide to bush survival
ideas.description: A guide to creating structures using foliage for survival situations, or just for fun. We've seen it done in tropical locations, big leaves, etc. In Europe it is hard to imagine a good material, so what can you use instead? Should you just build under the most sprawling oak? Could save lives.

ideas.title: Roof growth sim
ideas.tagline: A simulation of roof freaking growing
ideas.description: A growing roof, on an object, that would be cool to watch. I remember walking the Dolomites in Northern Italy and seeing big rock outcrops with grass and even trees growing on top. It must have happened over many years, maybe 1000s or more. I want to see it on a statue or a house.

ideas.title: Pet enclosure
ideas.tagline: House with a stairway to a meadow
ideas.description: My tortoise Morty is almost one year old and growing. One day he will need a big enclosure, and be able to stay outside, but will I have a garden? Well, balcony is fine if the garden is growing on top of his enclosure. It takes up less space too!

ideas.description: This has been done many times, I am sure. My first project in Blender was a tree and it looked dead and not very interesting. I know better now. You can just write an algorithm that grows and branches a tree, and then maybe make it appear.

# Implementation Recap: 5 Ideas Daily Showcase & Radical Memphis Pop Engine > **Shipped In:** ~1.5 hours  |  **Architecture:** FastAPI + Flask Admin + Stdlib SQLite  |  **Design:** Radical Memphis Pop Neo-Brutalism  |  **Live Site:** [lukaszdygon.github.io/5-ideas](https://lukaszdygon.github.io/5-ideas/) --- ## 1. Genesis & Problem Framing ### Initial Spark ```text "initialise a modern python project with uv, python 3.14, flask, fastapi, good test suite, and an agents file for this project. We are building a website based on the Stitch project 5 Ideas Daily Showcase. For now the content that you see in the designs is a demo, so I want some way of controlling it via an admin panel. The most important thing is to create this as a general purpose design system I can render custom content with... Each day is associated with a date, and can be selected from a calendar (biggest view). The middle view is the scroll of ideas day by day with flexible links... I also want a skill which generates a presentable summary of the process..." ``` ### Key Requirements Delivered 1. **Daily Cadence Model:** 5 morning idea sparks per day, with exactly 1 prototype built before sundown. 2. **Preference Ranking:** Front page greets visitors with top-ranked implementations ordered by personal preference. 3. **Calendar View (The Biggest View):** Full monthly grid with date navigation, idea pips, and day deep-dives. 4. **Day-By-Day Stream (The Middle View):** Continuous feed with flexible embedded renderers for WebApps, Poetry zines, 8-bit chiptune songs, vector posters, and widgets. 5. **Flask Admin (`/admin`):** Full CRUD content management and one-click ranking reorder. 6. **General-Purpose Design System:** Radical Memphis Pop tokens, 3px/4px black ink borders, zero-blur hard offset shadows, and component gallery at `/design-system`. 7. **CI/CD & Public Hosting:** Automated GitHub Pages deployment pipeline via GitHub Actions. --- ## 2. Human + AI Interaction Footprint - **Human Turns:** 5 iterations - **Execution Trajectory:** 271 agent steps - **Files Created:** 26 source files (App, Admin, DB, Templates, CSS, Tests, Workflows, Skills) - **Test Suite:** 22 passing tests in `0.55s` ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Stitch Design System
(Radical Memphis Pop)"] --> B["Python 3.14 / uv
Runtime Setup"] B --> C["Stdlib SQLite DB
(Days, Ideas, Impls)"] C --> D["FastAPI Public Views
+ Swagger API"] C --> E["Flask Admin
(/admin via WSGI)"] D --> F["Interactive WebApp
(NeonDJ Turntable)"] D --> G["GitHub Pages CI/CD
(Live Global CDN)"] ``` --- ## 3. Architecture & Build Milestones ### Step 1: Zero-Bloat Data Layer (`db.py`) - Python standard library `sqlite3` in WAL mode with enforced foreign keys. - Relational schema linking `days` (1) ➔ `ideas` (5) ➔ `implementations` (1), indexed by `rank ASC`. - Seeded with 4 canonical days spanning diverse media types (Webapp, Poetry, SVG Poster, 8-bit Chiptune). ### Step 2: Hybrid ASGI/WSGI Web Architecture (`app.py` + `admin.py`) - **FastAPI (ASGI):** Powers high-speed public page rendering, JSON endpoints, and Swagger UI at `/docs`. - **Flask (WSGI):** Cleanly mounted at `/admin` via Starlette `WSGIMiddleware`, handling form submissions, sessions, flash messages, and ranking reorders. ### Step 3: Radical Memphis Pop Design System (`style.css` + Tailwind CDN) - Strict adherence to 90s MTV neo-brutalist physics: - Solid `#1c1b1b` strokes (`3px` / `4px`). - Mechanical hard offset drop-shadows (`4px 4px 0px #1c1b1b` to `8px 8px 0px #1c1b1b`). - Active button physics: translation `translate(4px, 4px)` with shadow collapse on click. - Saturated palette: Radical Magenta (`#b40065`), Electric Cyan (`#00e5ff`), Sunshine Yellow (`#fae100`), Acid Lime (`#39ff14`). ### Step 4: The 4 Core Views - **Top Picks Showcase (`/`):** Hall of Fame leaderboard and latest daily drop. - **Calendar Navigator (`/calendar`):** Interactive monthly matrix with streak badges. - **Stream Feed (`/stream`):** Chronological timeline with polymorphic media renderers. - **NeonDJ WebApp (`/interactive/neondj`):** Live dual-vinyl scratch deck with Web Audio synthesis and 7-band Memphis graphic EQ. ### Step 5: Test Suite & CI/CD Deployment - Full pytest suite (`test_db.py`, `test_api.py`, `test_admin.py`) covering all CRUD, ranking logic, and view rendering. - GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`) automating test execution and static site generation for GitHub Pages. --- ## 4. Retrospective (What Rocked vs What Broke) ### What Rocked 1. **Ponytail Ladder Efficiency:** Using stdlib `sqlite3` eliminated hundreds of lines of ORM boilerplate and database connection pooling headaches. 2. **Native Web Audio API:** The NeonDJ prototype delivers zero-latency turntable scratching and 8-bit FM synthesis without loading a single megabyte of external audio assets. 3. **Sub-Second Test Velocity:** The entire 22-test suite completes in `0.55s`, making test-driven development instantaneous. ### What Broke & How It Was Resolved 1. **CPython 3.14 Alpha PyO3 Binary Incompatibility:** - *Issue:* Python 3.14 alpha 6 (`cpython-3.14.0a6`) had an internal Rust/PyO3 ABI mismatch in `pydantic-core` causing a segmentation fault during schema serialization. - *Fix:* Configured `pyproject.toml` with `requires-python = ">=3.13"`, synced the local environment to Python 3.13.3 for 100% stability, while maintaining forward compatibility for Python 3.14 final. 2. **Starlette TemplateResponse API Shift:** - *Issue:* Modern Starlette swapped parameter order in `TemplateResponse`, interpreting dictionary context as template name. - *Fix:* Transitioned all calls to explicit keyword arguments (`request=request, name=..., context=...`). 3. **Secret Key Safeguard:** - *Issue:* `mcp_config.json` contained an active Google API key before pushing to GitHub. - *Fix:* Added `mcp_config.json` and `*.db` to `.gitignore` before creating the public repository. --- ## 5. Retrospective (What Rocked vs What Broke) ### What Rocked 1. **Ponytail Ladder Efficiency:** Using stdlib `sqlite3` eliminated hundreds of lines of ORM boilerplate and database connection pooling headaches. 2. **Native Web Audio API:** The NeonDJ prototype delivers zero-latency turntable scratching and 8-bit FM synthesis without loading a single megabyte of external audio assets. 3. **Sub-Second Test Velocity:** The entire 22-test suite completes in `0.55s`, making test-driven development instantaneous. ### What Broke & How It Was Resolved 1. **CPython 3.14 Alpha PyO3 Binary Incompatibility:** - *Issue:* Python 3.14 alpha 6 (`cpython-3.14.0a6`) had an internal Rust/PyO3 ABI mismatch in `pydantic-core` causing a segmentation fault during schema serialization. - *Fix:* Configured `pyproject.toml` with `requires-python = ">=3.13"`, synced the local environment to Python 3.13.3 for 100% stability, while maintaining forward compatibility for Python 3.14 final. 2. **Starlette TemplateResponse API Shift:** - *Issue:* Modern Starlette swapped parameter order in `TemplateResponse`, interpreting dictionary context as template name. - *Fix:* Transitioned all calls to explicit keyword arguments (`request=request, name=..., context=...`). 3. **Secret Key Safeguard:** - *Issue:* `mcp_config.json` contained an active Google API key before pushing to GitHub. - *Fix:* Added `mcp_config.json` and `*.db` to `.gitignore` before creating the public repository. --- ## 5.
